newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen ends steady, sentiment bullish.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen ends steady, sentiment bullish.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen interest rate futures ended barely changed in lacklustre trade on Monday after tracking a confined range all day, traders said.
Sentiment is bullish, dealers said, but the contract is currently in technically overbought territory and likely to consolidate before making further gains.
The benchmark September Euroyen contract ended at 99.44 against its CME close at 99.43. An estimated 4,290 lots changed hands.

Dealers said the market had factored in last week's gloomy Tankan report and was now looking at the imminent release of a slate of U.S. economic indicators this week for signs of U.S. interest rate moves.

"The Euroyen is trading at the top now and if it goes up any further it may be for a another five to 10 points," said one dealer with a Japanese futures house. "The yen dealers are now looking out for the U.S. numbers because any U.S. hike will give the Bank Of Japan more room to raise rates," he added.
Dealers said the market was now scouting around for fresh factors before taking the Euroyen contract further.

Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended weaker from opening levels. Dealers said sentiment had been dented by market views that the Japanese financial half-year reporting season, due to begin soon, would yield a crop of poor results resulting in profit extraction in the JGBs.
Elsewhere, Eurodollar interest rate futures ended firmer after being held captive by the release of key data this week.
The jobless claims and payroll data on Friday and the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index on Tuesday is expected to bear on U.S. interest rate expectations.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.95 against their IMM close at 93.94. Some 2,950 lots changed hands. -- V.Lee(65 8703080)
